newsitem.title: USA: U.S. expects better cooperation from Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. expects better cooperation from Saudi Arabia.

text.p: The United States expects Saudi Arabia to cooperate with the investigation into the bombing that killed 19 American troops in that country, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Sunday.

She said on NBC television's "Meet the Press" programme that there was no disagreement with the Clinton administration regarding critical statements about Saudi cooperation from FBI Director Louis Freeh and Attorney General Janet Reno.

"The FBI is in charge of this investigation," Albright said. "The Saudis have been cooperative, but Mr. Freeh has asked for additional information. The Saudis have assured us at the highest levels that they will be cooperative, and we expect them to be cooperative."
"Mr. Freeh is in charge," she said. "There is a unified position within the United States government, and it is very important to us that this be resolved."
"I think we are a team and we have a unified team," Albright said.
The Saudi Embassy released a statement on Friday from Ambassador Prince Bandar Bin Sultan saying close cooperation between officials from both countries would continue.

It was issued after Freeh criticised Saudi Arabia for frustrating U.S. efforts to determine responsibility for the June 25 bombing in Dhahran. Reno joined Freeh in complaining that Saudi Arabia had failed to turn over key information.
Freeh's remarks, published in Thursday's Washington Post, were an unusually public criticism of a key ally.
Prince Bandar did not refer specifically to Freeh's comments, but issued his statement "in response to press inquiries."

"We have always reached agreement on a broad and significant range of issues. Excellent working relations exist between officials of both countries at all levels. That close cooperation will continue," he said.
